fullPassage:
It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc.

(A) If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
(B) One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison.
(C) We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way.

They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way.

questions.passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up. One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But <u>it doesn't always work this way</u>.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 it doesn't always work this way가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① '언제나 좋은 결과'는 'doesn't always'와 모순
❌ ② 실수의 효과는 오히려 긍정적(like better)이므로 부적절
❌ ③ '항상 선호한다'는 'doesn't always'와 모순
✅ ④ 유능한 사람 곁의 이점(better chance)이 항상 작동하지는 않는다는 의미. 뒤이어 너무 유능한 사람의 부정적 효과(uncomfortable)를 설명 ←정답
det.tip: But it doesn't always work this way — 유능한 사람 곁의 이점이 항상 적용되지는 않는다는 전환

ch: 유능한 사람은 언제나 좋은 결과를 만들어낸다.
